# REGIME READ — 2026-09-01

**[FULL-DATA READ]** WebSearch is available this run for the first time in four reads. All seven lenses now have live inputs — Positioning, Breadth and Sentiment have been dark since 2026-08-28 and are lit today. The option-chain block, which went missing last run, is also back (ATM IV, live spot, HV20, term ratio, put/call). **This is the best-informed read of the series, and it is the first one with a negative total.** Those two facts are connected: the previous +2 readings were computed on four lenses, three of which happened to be the calm ones.

**The single most important thing in this report is not in the local data at all.** The news daemon reports CAUTION at shock 15.0 and lists three tariff stories. It missed that **the United States and Iran resumed direct military exchanges overnight on 2026-08-31** — the first in more than a month — around a **Strait of Hormuz that has been effectively closed to commercial shipping since 2026-07-30**. That is what moved Brent, and it is why Lens 7 goes to its lowest reading of the series.

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage:** 3 (Neutral/choppy) → **3 (Neutral/choppy)** — unchanged, fourth consecutive read, but now sitting at the *bearish* edge of the stage rather than the middle. VIX 15.71 is still inside the 15–22 band that defines Stage 3, which is the only thing holding it there.
- **Total score:** +2 → **−2 (delta −4)**. The largest move of the series, and it is almost entirely a **data-availability** effect rather than a tape effect. Three lenses that were scored 0-by-default because they were dark now have real inputs: Breadth resolves to **−1**, Sentiment to **0**, Positioning stays **0** but for a measured reason. Lens 5 flips **+1 → −1** and Lens 7 **−1 → −2** on the Iran escalation. Read this as *the read getting more honest*, not as the market falling four points.
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 **and** VXN < 19:* **ARMED, both legs moved slightly away.** NDX 29,456.97 (2026-08-31) is **1.84% short** of 30,000. VXN 20.18 (2026-08-31) is **1.18 above** 19, versus 0.92 last read. Neither leg is close.
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **CLEARED.** NDX is 3.59% above the level.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ below the 50DMA two sessions, then below $70.00:* **ARMED — first leg has now engaged.** TQQQ closed **$71.92** on 2026-08-31 against a 50DMA of **$71.96**: below by **0.06%**. That is session one of the required two. A second sub-50DMA close arms the $70.00 leg, which sits 2.67% below spot. This is the only previous-read trigger that has actually begun to fire.
  - *Bearish — VXN > 25 with VIX/VIX3M ≥ 1.00:* **CLEARED, and now measurable again.** VXN 20.18; the term ratio is back at **0.851** (VIX 14.92 / VIX3M 17.53, 2026-08-31T20:45Z) — deep contango, meaning near-dated volatility is priced *below* longer-dated. Both legs fail comfortably.
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25%:* **CLEARED and improved.** HY OAS **2.60%** (2026-08-28), tighter than last read's 2.63%.
  - *Neutralizer — IV/HV below 0.85 (hostile) or above 1.25 (favourable):* **RESTORED, and it fired in neither direction.** IV/HV prints **1.00** (ATM IV 55.0% vs HV20 54.5%). The series now reads 1.02 → 0.94 → *blind* → **1.00**. Last read I said the blind print must not be treated as recovered; it turns out it did recover, back to exact parity. I honour that threshold both ways: **the premium environment is neutral, not hostile.**
- **Notable lens flips:** Lens 4 Breadth **0 → −1** (now measured: NYSE decliners led advancers 1.95-to-1 on 2026-08-31). Lens 5 Cross-asset **+1 → −1** (see the correction below). Lens 7 Geopolitical **−1 → −2** (Iran military exchange + Hormuz closure + China trade). Lens 2 holds **+1**, Lens 3 holds **+1**.

**Correction to last read's Lens 5 reasoning.** I scored cross-assets **+1** on the argument that soft energy plus tight credit reads as disinflationary. That interpretation was wrong, and web access shows why: Brent's 52-week high of **126.10** was set during the earlier phase of the Iran conflict, so "Brent 29% below its 52-week high" was never evidence of *softness* — it was a war spike decaying. With the US and Iran exchanging fire again and Brent turning back up **+1.60%**, the correct reading is a live supply-shock risk, not disinflation. Lens 5 goes to **−1**.

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy.** VIX 15.71 (2026-09-01) and VXN 20.18 (2026-08-31) sit inside the 15–22 band; indices are 1.7–4.2% below 52-week highs; credit spreads are tight, not stressed. Stage 4 (regime-change) requires VIX in the 20–30 range and rising; VIX at 15.71 fails that plainly, even though the breadth-deterioration half of the Stage-4 description is now satisfied.
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-31 — the Iran/Hormuz re-escalation**, replacing the previous placeholder anchor of the 2026-08-27 NVDA reaction. This is the first read in the series with a properly dated anchor event. Broader context: the conflict phase began **2026-02-28** when the US and Israel began attacking Iran (matching the template's own "Feb'26 risk-off (Iran war)" marker), and the Strait has been effectively shut since **2026-07-30**.
- **Position:** Week 1 of a re-escalation leg, inside a Stage-3 range that has now been confirmed across four consecutive reads (2026-08-28, 08-29, 08-31, 09-01). Minimum observed Stage-3 duration is 4 sessions. Note August finished as an *up* month — Nasdaq roughly +3.9%, Dow's fifth straight monthly gain — so the chop has had an upward tilt until this week.
- **Confidence:** **Low** — and for the opposite reason to previous reads. Data availability is the best of the series (7 of 7 lenses live). Confidence is Low because the lenses genuinely **disagree**: the largest aligned bloc is 3 bearish (Breadth, Cross-asset, Geopolitical) against 2 bullish (Dealer flow, Macro) and 2 neutral. Credit and the volatility term structure say calm; participation and geopolitics say deteriorating. That is real uncertainty, not missing information.
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ 30,000 (+1.84%) **with** VXN < 19. Both legs.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above 20 **or** VXN > 25; **or** NDX < 28,400 (−3.59%); **or** HY OAS widening through 3.25% from 2.60%; **or** the VIX/VIX3M term ratio rising through 1.00 from 0.851 (backwardation — near-term risk repricing above longer-term, the classic shock signature).

## Regime Verdict
A low-volatility, tight-credit Stage-3 range that is quietly deteriorating underneath — narrowing participation, an active US–Iran military exchange at a closed oil chokepoint, and a live trade-policy thread — held together by a calm volatility surface that has not yet repriced, at **Low** confidence because the lenses genuinely conflict.

## Diverging Signals

**The defining tension is that the price of risk and the quantity of risk are pointing in opposite directions.** The two bullish lenses are both measures of what risk *costs*: credit spreads at 2.60%/0.79% and a volatility term structure in deep contango at 0.851. The three bearish lenses are all measures of how much risk *exists*: narrowing participation, a kinetic conflict at a closed oil chokepoint, and an unresolved trade escalation. Markets can hold that combination for a long time. What it means concretely for anyone underwriting downside is that the compensation on offer is being set by the calm half of the picture while the hazard is being set by the other half.

**Second: the local news feed and reality diverged, and this is a process finding, not a market one.** The daemon reported **CAUTION / 15.0** with three tariff stories and did not surface a resumption of US–Iran military strikes, a US attack on Larak Island, Iranian missiles landing near US forces in Jordan and the UAE, or an attempted mining of the Strait of Hormuz. Every one of those is squarely inside the "Iran/Israel/Russia/Taiwan geopolitical escalation" category the scoring rules weight **2×**. Three prior reads scored Lens 7 at −1 partly on the daemon's own output. **On a WebSearch-less run, this read would have scored Lens 7 at −1 and published a total of −1 or 0 while a shooting war escalated.** That is the most actionable item in this report.

**Third: SKEW is the one gauge that was right early.** SKEW has now printed 144.05 → **148.53**, rising while VIX sat in the mid-14s. For two reads I flagged it as the dissenting voice under a calm surface. With Brent +3% on a military exchange and VIX +5.29% the next session, the persistent bid for far-out-of-the-money crash protection looks less like noise. VVIX +4.09% and MOVE +7.82% in the same session point the same way.

**Fourth: TQQQ is flat on a down day for its own index, and the vol data is a session behind the escalation.** TQQQ printed **+0.10%** on 2026-08-31 while NDX printed **−0.62%** — for a 3× fund those should differ by roughly 1.9 percentage points, and they do not. Two independent sources (the bar feed and the 20:45Z chain snapshot) agree TQQQ is **$71.92**, and the previous read's chain gave **$71.85** on 2026-08-28, so the *level* is solid; it is the NDX day-change alignment that does not reconcile, and I cannot resolve which side is off. Separately, **ATM IV 55.0% is stamped 2026-08-31T20:45Z — before the Sep-1 session in which VIX rose 5.29%.** So the IV/HV = 1.00 reading is a *pre-repricing* number. Premium is probably richer today than this report says; that is not good news, because the reason is that risk repriced.

**Fifth: the Aug-31 breadth is worse than the index prints suggest.** SPX fell 0.33% and Nasdaq Composite 0.12% on the day, while decliners beat advancers roughly 2-to-1 on the NYSE. A handful of very large names held the indices up. That is the same concentration point the Magnificent-Seven-at-63%-of-NDX figure makes from the other direction.

## TQQQ Read

- **Momentum: neutral, and stubbornly so.** RSI(14) at **47.1** is barely changed from 47.0 and has sat mid-range for four reads. For a put seller this remains the least informative state — no overbought stretch to fade, no washed-out low offering fat premium plus a mean-reversion tailwind. The streak is **0 red / 1 green**, a single flat-to-up day (+0.10%) rather than any kind of run. There is no momentum signal here in either direction.

- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS — both tests measured against a live spot.** **DOWNTURN fails on both legs:** spot is **7.68% below** the 4-week high of $77.90 (needs >20%), and VXN 20.18 is well under the ≥25 requirement. **RALLY fails:** spot is **5.87% above** the 4-week low of $67.93 (71.92 / 67.93 − 1), far short of the >30% required. So **SIDEWAYS**. Note the RALLY margin has collapsed from 17.5% last read to 5.87% — not because price fell much, but because the 4-week low rolled up $5.54. The classification is unchanged; the distance to it moved a lot.

- **Trend: intact on the long horizon, exactly balanced on the medium one.** Spot is **+17.9% above the 200DMA (~$61.00)** — a genuine, wide cushion and the single most robust bullish fact about the instrument. Against the **50DMA at $71.96**, spot closed **0.06% below**, which resolves last read's ambiguity in the mildly negative direction: TQQQ is no longer above its 50-day line. One close does not make a trend, and 0.06% is inside noise — but it is the first leg of the two-session bearish trigger I set last read, and it is worth watching precisely because it is unambiguous rather than because it is large.

- **Volatility & premium environment: fairly priced, with a stale timestamp.** **ATM IV 55.0% against HV20 54.5% gives IV/HV = 1.00.** In plain terms: options are priced at almost exactly what TQQQ has actually been moving, so a seller collects the fair-coin price and no more — there is no variance risk premium, the extra compensation a seller normally earns for underwriting uncertainty. This is a *recovery* from last read's known trajectory (1.02 → 0.94 → blind → 1.00) and it does not breach the 0.85 hostile threshold I named. In **absolute** terms premium is on the low side: VXN 20.18 is 41.3% below its 52-week high, and the term structure at 0.851 is in deep contango, meaning the market is charging *less* for near-dated risk than for longer-dated. The important qualifier: **all of that is stamped 2026-08-31, before VIX rose 5.29% on 2026-09-01.** VXN and TQQQ IV are almost certainly higher today than these figures show, so the live premium is probably better than 55% — but realized volatility will likely rise too, and whether IV/HV improved cannot be known from this run's data.

- **Put-selling context: CAUTIOUS.** The supportive facts are real and I am not discounting them: credit spreads are tight and *tighter* than last read (HY 2.60%, IG 0.79%), the curve is normally sloped at +0.41%, the volatility term structure is in deep contango at 0.851, price is 17.9% above its 200-day average, and IV/HV at 1.00 is fair rather than punitive. Against that, four things argue for restraint, and they are about the hazard side rather than the price side. First, **the US and Iran are exchanging fire again at a Strait of Hormuz that is already closed** — an unscheduled, unpriced gap source with no visible resolution path, and one the local news feed did not detect. Second, **participation is narrowing** — roughly 2-to-1 decliners on the NYSE while the indices barely moved, A/D lines back at their 50-day averages, and 63% of NDX in seven names. Third, **NFP lands 2026-09-04, inside the window**, three sessions before a long weekend and eight before a live FOMC that markets price near a coin flip. Fourth, **IV/HV at exactly 1.00 means there is no cushion**: a seller is being paid the fair price of ordinary movement while underwriting three concurrent, non-ordinary gap sources. The reason this is CAUTIOUS rather than HOSTILE is that the one threshold I committed to in advance — IV/HV below 0.85 — did not print; premium is fair, not stolen. What would flip it hostile: IV/HV falling back below 0.85, **or** the term ratio rising through 1.00 (near-dated risk repricing above longer-dated), **or** a second sub-50DMA close followed by a break of $70.00. Context only — no strikes, expiries, sizes, or trade calls.

## Forward Levels & Triggers
- **Bullish trigger:** NDX reclaims **30,000** (+1.84%) **and** VXN closes below **19** (currently 20.18).
